system_description.narrative_title: Interlinked Crises: AI-led Markets, Geopolitical Realignments, and Social Unrest
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is operating as a tightly coupled open system in flux where an AI-driven investment and infrastructure boom collides with rising borrowing costs and insurance/credit stress, while major-power diplomacy and regional conflicts reshape alignments. Simultaneously, energy-price shocks and inflationary pressures amplify domestic political unrest across advanced and emerging economies, creating feedback loops between markets, governments and security dynamics. The result is heightened systemic fragility: cascades in financial markets, contested tech and data infrastructure, and opportunistic geopolitical manoeuvres that together reshape short- and medium-term risk calculus.
system_description.scope: Nation-states, major-power diplomacy, regional conflicts (Ukraine, Middle East, Israel/Palestine), global financial markets and credit instruments, technology and AI firms and infrastructure (data centres, chip industry, AI startups), energy and commodity flows, and mass social/political movements and protests
system_description.super_system: The planetary international political-economic-security system (the global socio-technical-economic order)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial system and credit markets
Energy and commodities system (oil, diesel, gas)
Technology & AI infrastructure ecosystem (chips, data centres, cloud)
Regional security complexes (Europe, Middle East, Eastern Europe/Central Asia)

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine war and diplomacy
variables.description: Russia, Ukraine and Western backers are locked in sustained military confrontation even as selective diplomacy and envoy-led talks create shifting prospects for ceasefires, territorial control and negotiated settlements.

variables.name: Iran-led regional escalation
variables.description: Iran, its proxies (notably the Houthis), Saudi Arabia, Israel and other regional actors are driving an intensifying campaign of strikes on shipping and infrastructure that risks wider military escalation and diplomatic fragmentation across the Gulf and Levant.

variables.name: US–China technology and data rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting market access, standards, industrial policy and data governance for advanced technologies, as each side increases state intervention to secure strategic tech advantage and supply chains.

variables.name: AI infrastructure build-out and financial risk
variables.description: A rapid private-sector AI and compute build-out is concentrating capital and operational risk in data‑centre capacity, equities, credit and insurance markets, producing systemic strains and shifting economic power toward compute-intensive actors.

variables.name: US political volatility and foreign-policy shifts
variables.description: Domestic political turbulence in the United States—driven by electoral cycles, high-profile personnel churn and a highly personalized White House—produces abrupt foreign-policy swings that recalibrate alliance behavior, security commitments and global credibility.
